jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

About The Role

Peraton is seeking a mid-level All Source Intelligence Analyst
to provide analysis of multi-INT data to develop comprehensive and accurate identity intelligence on behalf of a national-level customer. The analyst will evaluate diverse datasets and produce specialized intelligence products and briefings for a variety of stakeholders, including internal and external partners as well as senior policymakers. The ideal candidate has experience supporting the intelligence and/or law enforcement communities, strong attention to detail, and the ability to perform independently and within a team in a fast-paced environment under minimal supervision.

Key Responsibilities
of this role include:

Integrating and analyzing disparate, raw data and semi-structured reports to uncover patterns and trends, developing actionable intelligence to inform and disrupt;
Developing, coordinating, incorporating feedback within, and delivering all-source intelligence products, targeting products, and/or briefings;
Ensuring all products adhere to applicable customer and community standards;
Maintaining quality standards as directed by the program leadership team and supporting the implementation of corrective actions as needed;
Engaging with colleagues to support initiatives designed to enhance customer tools and close capabilities gaps

#MissionIntel

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Current TS/SCI clearance with polygraph;
Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of relevant experience, 4 years of additional relevant experience may be considered in lieu of degree;
Experience leveraging analytic methodologies and tradecraft, and ability to apply those skills within the intelligence cycle;
Familiarity with the use of visual analysis tools to support the development of data-driven products;
Strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills;
Ability to effectively communicate with diverse technical and non-technical audiences;
Ability to apply critical thinking skills to resolve issues with support from leadership

Desired Qualifications

Experience supporting national-level customers;
Experience working in the customer's operational environment;
Experience leveraging customer tools and databases to develop analytic products

Details

Target Salary Range: $86,000 - $138,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual's experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

Benefits Statement: Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

Application Statements: The application period for the job is estimated to be 30 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. By applying to this job, you are expressing interest in the role and the Company. During the review of your application, you may be required to participate in an on-camera interview, as well as participate in a process to verify your identity. Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools of any kind during Peraton interviews is strictly prohibited unless the candidate has obtained prior written authorization. All interview responses must be the candidate's own.

jobs.description:
Marketing Data Analyst

Location:
Brickell, Miami, FL
Employment Type:
Full-Time
Department:
Marketing
Turn Data Into Decisions. Turn Marketing Investment Into Measurable Growth.

The Ferraro Law Firm, P.A. is seeking a highly analytical and technically skilled Senior Marketing Data Analyst / Business Intelligence Analyst
to transform complex marketing, intake, and client acquisition data into actionable business intelligence.

This is not a traditional marketing reporting role.

We are looking for someone who can build the infrastructure and analysis necessary to answer the questions that matter:
Where are our best cases coming from? Which campaigns generate qualified leads and signed clients? What does it cost to acquire a case? Where are leads being lost? Which marketing investments should we increase, decrease, or eliminate?

The ideal candidate can work across multiple data sources—including advertising platforms, web analytics, call tracking, CRM/case-management systems, and intake data—to create a reliable picture of performance from marketing spend through signed case and business outcome.

What You'll Own

Marketing & Client Acquisition Analytics
Analyze performance across paid search, paid social, SEO, organic, referral, television, digital, and other client acquisition channels.
Build reporting that connects the full acquisition funnel:

Marketing Spend → Lead → Qualified Lead → Intake → Consultation → Signed Case → Case Type/Value

Measure lead quality—not simply lead volume—across campaigns, channels, vendors, geographies, keywords, and practice areas.
Analyze cost and conversion performance by campaign and acquisition source.
Identify underperforming marketing investments and opportunities to improve ROI.
Conduct cohort, funnel, trend, and segmentation analyses to identify patterns in client acquisition.
Partner with Marketing and Intake leadership to determine why qualified leads are converting—or being lost.

Business Intelligence & Dashboard Development
Design, build, and maintain executive dashboards using Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, or similar BI platforms
.
Develop dashboards that provide leadership with real-time visibility into marketing spend, lead generation, intake performance, signed cases, and acquisition costs.
Automate recurring reporting and reduce dependence on manual spreadsheet-based analysis.
Establish standardized KPI definitions and reporting methodologies across Marketing and Intake.
Develop reporting that allows leadership to drill down from firm-wide performance to individual campaigns, sources, markets, and practice areas.

Attribution & ROI Analysis
Develop and improve marketing attribution models across multiple channels and client touchpoints.
Connect advertising and lead-source data to CRM and case-management records.
Analyze the relationship between marketing investment and actual signed cases.
Evaluate campaign performance based on business outcomes rather than clicks, impressions, or surface-level lead volume
.
Develop methodologies for measuring customer/client acquisition cost, return on ad spend, and marketing ROI.
Identify attribution gaps and recommend improvements to tracking architecture.

Data Analysis & Infrastructure
Use SQL
to query, combine, validate, and analyze data from multiple sources.
Integrate and reconcile information from platforms such as:
Salesforce / Litify
Google Analytics 4
Google Ads
Meta Ads
Call-tracking platforms
Intake systems
Internal databases and spreadsheets
Identify data-quality issues, duplicate records, attribution inconsistencies, and tracking gaps.
Partner with internal stakeholders and external vendors to improve data integrity.
Create repeatable processes for extracting, transforming, validating, and analyzing marketing and intake data.
Maintain documentation for reporting logic, KPI definitions, and data sources.

Core KPIs
The Senior Marketing Data Analyst will help establish, monitor, and improve metrics including:
Marketing Spend
Cost per Lead (CPL)
Cost per Qualified Lead
Cost per Consultation
Cost per Signed Case / Client Acquisition Cost
Lead-to-Qualified Conversion Rate
Qualified Lead-to-Signed-Case Conversion Rate
Overall Lead-to-Signed-Case Conversion Rate
Intake Conversion Rate
Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)
Marketing ROI
Lead Quality by Source
Signed Cases by Campaign
Acquisition Cost by Practice Area
Funnel Leakage / Lost Lead Analysis

What We're Looking For
Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Marketing Analytics, Computer Science
, or a related quantitative discipline.
3+ years of experience
in marketing analytics, business intelligence, performance analytics, or a comparable data-driven role.
Strong SQL skills and demonstrated ability to work with large, complex datasets.
Advanced proficiency with Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or comparable BI/data visualization platforms
.
Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets skills.
Experience with Google Analytics 4 and digital advertising data
.
Strong understanding of marketing attribution, conversion funnels, CAC/CPA, CPL, ROAS, and ROI.
Experience combining data from multiple systems and identifying inconsistencies between data sources.
Experience with Salesforce, Litify, or another CRM/case-management platform strongly preferred.
Familiarity with call tracking and lead attribution platforms is highly desirable.
Python or R experience is a plus.
Experience with APIs, ETL processes, data warehouses, or cloud-based analytics environments is a plus.
Experience in legal marketing, personal injury, mass torts, lead generation, healthcare, insurance, or another high-value consumer acquisition industry
is highly desirable.

This Is Not a Reporting-Only Position
We are not looking for someone whose primary function is exporting reports and distributing spreadsheets.

We need an analyst who will interrogate the data.

When CPL increases, you investigate why.
When lead volume increases but signed cases decline, you identify where the funnel is breaking.
When two platforms report different conversion numbers, you determine which data is reliable.
When a campaign generates inexpensive leads but poor-quality cases, you make that visible.
When the data identifies an opportunity, you communicate it clearly enough for leadership to act.
Your responsibility is not simply to tell us what happened.

Your responsibility is to help us understand why it happened, what it means, and what we should investigate or change next.

Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by the analyst's ability to:
Produce accurate, reliable, and actionable business intelligence.
Improve visibility into the firm's true cost of client acquisition.
Establish reliable attribution from marketing source through signed case.
Identify opportunities to improve marketing efficiency and conversion.
Detect weaknesses within the Marketing-to-Intake funnel.
Reduce manual reporting through dashboarding and automation.
Improve data quality and confidence in executive reporting.
Deliver insights that influence marketing investment decisions.
Communicate complex findings clearly to senior leadership.
Proactively identify trends, risks, and opportunities before being asked.

Who Will Succeed Here
You are highly analytical, naturally skeptical of incomplete data, and comfortable digging until you understand what is actually happening.
You don't confuse more leads
with better marketing
.
You understand that a campaign generating 500 leads may be less valuable than one generating 50 highly qualified cases.

You are equally comfortable building a SQL query, analyzing a conversion funnel, creating an executive dashboard, and explaining your conclusions to someone who doesn't work in analytics.
You take ownership of the accuracy of your work and understand that leadership may make significant investment decisions based on the information you provide.

About The Ferraro Law Firm, P.A.
The Ferraro Law Firm, P.A. is a plaintiff-side law firm representing individuals and families in significant personal injury, catastrophic injury, and mass tort matters.
As our marketing and client acquisition operations continue to evolve, we are investing in stronger analytics and business intelligence capabilities to ensure our decisions are driven by reliable data, measurable performance, and actual business outcomes.

Altair Data Resources is seeking a Data Analyst with professional experience in data processing, analysis, and automation who is looking for an opportunity to work in an entrepreneurial, high-growth, collaborative environment. This role emphasizes Python, SQL, and extract, transform, and load (ETL) workflows to process, validate, analyze, and deliver data. You will also leverage AI-assisted tools to improve productivity, support problem-solving, and automate routine tasks. Supporting technologies may include Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, and other data processing and visualization tools.

Data Analyst Job Duties

Data Analyst responsibilities include conducting analysis and producing accurate datasets based on customer or management requirements. You will develop and maintain data processing workflows, use Python and SQL to automate recurring tasks, and support analysis and reporting capabilities. You will also troubleshoot data issues, monitor data quality and process performance, and identify opportunities for improvement.

Data Analyst Responsibilities

Develop and maintain Python scripts and SQL queries to extract, transform, analyze, and deliver data.
Build, maintain, and troubleshoot ETL workflows that combine data from multiple sources, apply business rules, and prepare datasets for analysis or client delivery.
Acquire data from primary and secondary sources and maintain databases and data processing systems.

Clean, validate, and reconcile data to identify errors, resolve inconsistencies, and ensure accuracy and completeness.
Use company-approved AI tools to assist with coding, troubleshooting, documentation, and process improvement while validating outputs and following data security and confidentiality requirements.
Document workflows, business rules, and quality control procedures to support reliable and repeatable processing.
Work with management and internal teams to understand requirements, prioritize business needs, and deliver accurate results within established timelines.
Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, improve data quality, and increase processing efficiency.

At least two years of professional experience in data analysis, data processing, ETL development, or a related role.
Practical experience using Python for data cleaning, transformation, and automation. Familiarity with data processing libraries such as pandas is preferred.
Strong working knowledge of SQL, including joins, filters, aggregations, and queries involving multiple tables.
Experience developing or maintaining ETL workflows and working with relational databases, structured data files, and data quality controls.
Ability to troubleshoot processing failures, investigate data discrepancies, and implement reliable solutions.
Familiarity with Excel and reporting or visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI. Alteryx experience is a plus but is not required.

Strong analytical and organizational skills, basic knowledge of statistics, and attention to detail when working with large datasets.

jobs.title: Senior Information Security Analyst
jobs.description:
As a Senior Information Security Analyst
, you will act as an advisor and security subject matter expert supporting government partners. You will be interested in partnering with business leaders, technical teams, customers, and external stakeholders to identify risks, implement effective controls, and drive continuous improvement. To support this, a strong understanding of NIST, HIPAA, and/or state laws would be beneficial.

Success in this role requires a deep understanding of cybersecurity principles, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent communication abilities, and the adaptability to navigate a dynamic regulatory and threat landscape. Ideally, you will be a collaborative leader who excels at translating complex security concepts into practical business solutions.

Candidates for this position will be required to be 100% onsite in either our West Des Moines, Iowa location, or our greater Chicago area location.

What You'll Do:

Governance, Risk, and Compliance

Evaluates organizational compliance with contractual regulatory, and state security requirements. Supports gap and risk remediation
Develops and implements security standards and procedures to safeguard resources ensuring compliance with HIPAA, NIST, FedRAMP and/or HITRUST requirements
Evaluates security risks balancing business drivers, best practices and external drivers. Provides proactive solutions or recommendations through collaboration across business units
Participates in development, review, and maintenance of System Security Plans (SSPs), security policies, standards, and procedures
Supports annual assessments and security authorization activities
Prepares reports for management detailing the status of security incidents, audit findings, and risk assessments

Security Operations and Vulnerability Management

Supports vulnerability management activities. Validates creation, documentation, and completion of Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms)
Participates in incident investigations, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and lessons learned activities
Coordinates breach notification activities and security reporting in accordance with contractual and regulatory requirements

Collaboration and Communication

Owns and delivers tasks on projects for the security team and with internal customer projects. Ensures timely completion of deliverables
Represents security on initiatives across Telligen. Works closely with internal customers to ensure implementation of security controls and best practices
Stays current with industry trends, emerging threats, security technologies, and pertinent regulations
Provides guidance and mentorship to other members of the security team
Provides timely responses, uses professional communication, and approaches vulnerability and risk management from the perspective of business enablement

Required Skills and Experience:

2-year degree in Information Technology, Information Security, or related field and/or equivalent training and/or experience
5-7 years of work experience in IT; 3 or more years of experience must be in an information security role with demonstrated working knowledge of information security, federal and state rules and regulations, company/business unit operations, compliance policies, procedures, and/or programs in area of assignment

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, MIS, Information Assurance or related field is preferred
CISSP, CISM, CISA, GSNA, CCSP, Security+, or equivalent industry certification preferred
Experience with NIST, ISO, and HIPAA requirements/guidance is highly desirable

Who We Are:

Telligen is one of the most respected population health management organizations in the country. We offer clinical, analytical, and technical expertise to support local, Tribal, and national partners, state and federal government programs, and employers and health plans.

Over our 50-year history, health care has evolved - and so have we. What hasn't changed is our deep commitment to those we serve. Our success is built on our ability to adapt, respond to client needs and deliver innovative, mission-driven solutions.

Our business is our people and we’re seeking talented individuals who share our passion and are ready to take ownership, make an impact and help shape the future of health.

Are you Ready?

We’re on a mission to transform lives and economies by improving health.

Ownership:
As a 100% employee-owned company, our employee-owners drive our business and share in our success.

Community:
We show up - for our clients, our communities and each other. Being a responsible corporate partner is part of who we are.

Ingenuity:
We value bold ideas and calculated risks. Innovation thrives when we challenge the status quo and listen to diverse perspectives.

Integrity:
We foster a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative environment built on trust and excellence.

Thank you for your interest in Telligen!

Follow us on Twitter, Facebook, and LinkedIn to learn more about our mission-driven culture and stay up to speed.

Brief Job Description

Are you a highly motivated, compassionate and dedicated individual looking for a rewarding career assisting the most vulnerable citizens of Texas in need of food, medical care, cash assistance and other social services?

If so, the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) Access and Eligibility Services (AES) division is looking for individuals who want to join an exciting, dynamic team working in a high-performing and innovative environment. AES provides an integrated and streamlined approach to connect individuals to services and supports that: reduce institutionalization, allow individuals to remain in their communities, and promote economic and personal self-sufficiency. AES is built upon its’ core values of respect, ownership, collaboration, and integrity with a goal of delivering best-in-class customer service to clients and stakeholders.

Our staff are well organized, able to multi-task, possess the ability to learn policy regulations, able to thrive in a challenging, fast-paced, and evolving environment, have good communication skills, a positive attitude, strong work-ethic and a desire to help others. If you also possess these skills, then we are looking for you.

We want you to join our team!

The Program Manager manages eligibility unit supervisors at benefit offices and out stationed sites. Responsible for providing program and technical assistance, as well as coaching and development of team supervisors, workers, and clerical staff. Work involves planning, developing, implementing, and monitoring Access and Eligibility Services programs. Works under general direction with extensive latitude for use of initiative and independent judgment. Job requires highly driven individuals with a high degree of ethics and integrity, good communication, interpersonal and analytical skills, and the ability to make effective decisions. This position may require up to 40% of travel.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Manages operations to ensure delivery of eligibility services in a timely and accurate manner according to state and federal regulations.

Develops and maintains systems to monitor operations and ensure compliance with policies and procedures in assigned area.

Collects, organizes, analyzes, and prepares material in response to requests for information, complaints, and reports.

Review and approves all staffing and personnel actions, evaluates program operations to recommend modifications and develop efficiencies when needed and provides a variety of narrative and statistical reports regarding performance standards and staffing needs.

Works with the general public, regional management, and State Office staff to resolve inquiries/issues in an effective and timely manner.

Participates in program analysis with regional management staff.

Selects, manages, and develops staff through conferences, mentoring, training, and performance appraisal.

Manages time and leave, payroll, and personnel actions.

Must be able to work occasional overtime, as required by management, outside of normal hours of operation, which may include weekends when called upon.

Must be able to work in a demanding, rapid-paced and developing environment.

Knowledge Of

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSAs):

Local, state, and federal laws and regulations related to agency programs.
Cash Assistance, SNAP (Food Stamps), and/or medical eligibility programs, including Medicaid for the elderly and people with disabilities, pregnant women, families, and/or children.

Skill In

Managing customer service operations and supervising staff.
Making decisions and solving problems involving varied levels of complexity, ambiguity, and risk
Selecting, managing, and developing staff.
Monitoring and evaluating unit performance and developing appropriate corrective action plans.
Training, directing and monitoring the work of others.
Communicating effectively, orally and in writing.
Operating a personal computer and use of software such as Microsoft Office applications.

Ability To

Establish and maintain effective monitoring systems.
Develop and evaluate administrative policies and procedures.
Develop and establish effective working relationships.
Plan, organize, assign, and monitor work.
Gather, assemble, correlate, and analyze facts.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

N/A

Initial Screening Criteria

High School diploma or GED equivalent is required.

Sixty (60) semester hours from an accredited college or university is required. Two (2) years of customer service experience may be substituted for required education.

A Degree from an accredited college or university is preferred.

A minimum of two (2) years’ experience, gained within the last 5 years’, in supervising a SNAP, Medicaid, Medicaid for the Elderly and People with Disabilities (MEPD) or Cash Assistance program/unit.

Current experience within two (2) years in SNAP, Medicaid, Medicaid for the Elderly and People with Disabilities (MEPD), Cash Assistance or other Medicaid programs.

Experience in planning, developing, implementing, and monitoring individual or unit performance improvement plans to enhance employee or unit performance.

Experience leading, mentoring, or motivating staff with varied skill levels and experience.

Experience using computer software such as Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

Texas Integrated Eligibility Redesign System (TIERS) and Eligibility Workload Management System (EWMS) experience is preferred.

Application indicates the willingness to work beyond normal work hours of 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM.

Application indicates the willingness to travel.

Additional Information

Access and Eligibility Services Field Office normal hours of operation are Monday-Friday 8:00am to 5:00pm. Employees may be required to work overtime, as required by management, outside of normal hours of operation, which may include weekends.

Role description

Under general direction of the AirTrain Director, this position is responsible for the comprehensive management and administration of all AirTrain safety and security programs in compliance with 49 CFR Part 659 (Rail Fixed Guideway Systems – State Safety Oversight), California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) General Order 164-B, and the AirTrain Public Transit Agency Safety Plan (PTASP).

The position serves as the primary liaison with internal Airport departments and external agencies, including Airport Safety and Health, Aviation Security, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and the Rail Operations and Regulatory Commission (ROAR), to ensure continuous awareness of changes to state and federal safety and security regulations. This position is responsible for integrating all applicable regulatory updates into the AirTrain PTASP and related operating procedures.

Through the execution of ongoing audits, inspections, and procedural reviews, this role ensures that AirTrain operations and maintenance activities are conducted in full accordance with established rules, standards, and regulatory requirements. The position is also responsible for investigating, documenting, and formally reporting all safety and security incidents or violations to the CPUC, as required by the PTASP, CPUC General Order 164-B, and other applicable regulations.

In coordination with local, state, and federal emergency response agencies, the position develops, maintains, and exercises emergency preparedness and response strategies, including the planning and execution of tabletop and full-scale emergency exercises.

As a key member of the AirTrain management team, this position contributes to daily system oversight by monitoring operational performance, identifying emerging risks or deficiencies, and initiating appropriate corrective actions to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant system operations.

The essential functions of this position include, but are not limited to, the following:

Plan, develop, implement, and administer AirTrain safety and security programs in compliance with 49 CFR Part 659, CPUC General Order 164-B, and the AirTrain Public Transit Agency Safety Plan (PTASP).
Work with the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) and other safety and security agencies to keep abreast of changes in state and federal regulations impacting the AirTrain. Identify and analyze corrective actions that must be incorporated into the AirTrain PTASP.
Maintain, update, and ensure implementation of the AirTrain PTASP and related safety and security policies, procedures, and manuals.
Monitor changes in federal and state safety and security regulations and ensure timely incorporation into AirTrain programs and operating practices.
Serve as the primary liaison with internal Airport departments and external agencies, including Airport Safety and Health, Aviation Security, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the CPUC, and the Rail Operations and Regulatory Commission (ROAR).
Conduct and oversee safety and security audits, inspections, investigations, and procedural reviews to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and industry standards.
Investigate safety and security incidents, hazards, and rule violations; prepare required documentation; and submit formal reports to the CPUC and other regulatory agencies as required.
Develop, coordinate, and evaluate emergency preparedness and response plans in collaboration with emergency response agencies.
Plan, conduct, and evaluate tabletop and full-scale emergency exercises and drills.
Monitor daily AirTrain operational performance from a safety and security perspective and initiate corrective actions when unsafe or non-compliant conditions are identified.
Participate as a member of the AirTrain management team, providing safety and security expertise in operational decision-making and system planning.
Provide on call duty 24/7 and represents the AirTrain Director during emergencies which occur after normal working hours, including holidays and weekends.
Assist AirTrain Director in other projects as required.
Perform other duties as assigned.

How to qualify

Qualifications

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university. AND
Experience: Four (4) years of professional level experience in transit operations administration, and/or transit safety and security management.

Education Substitution
: Additional qualifying experience as described above may be substituted for the required degree on a year-for-year basis (up to the maximum of 2 years). Thirty (30) semester units or forty-five (45) quarter units equal one year.

Desirable Qualifications

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred to hiring.

Experience in rail transit, automated people mover (APM), or airport transportation systems, including familiarity with guideway operations, vehicle systems, and integrated station environments.
Demonstrated knowledge of rail and transit safety regulatory frameworks, including Federal Transit Administration (FTA) requirements, 49 CFR Part 673, 49 CFR Part 659, and applicable state oversight programs such as California Public Utilities Commission's (CPUC) General Order 164-B.
Experience developing, implementing, or managing a Public Transportation Agency Safety Plan (PTASP) or similar safety management framework.
Working knowledge of Safety Management Systems (SMS) principles, including hazard identification, risk assessment, safety assurance, and safety promotion.
Experience coordinating safety investigations and root cause analyses related to operational incidents, equipment failures, or infrastructure conditions.
Familiarity with transit or rail security practices, including coordination with airport security, law enforcement agencies, and emergency management partners.
Experience developing safety procedures, operating rules, and compliance programs within a complex operational environment.
Strong collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with operations, maintenance, engineering, regulatory agencies, and external contractors.
Experience supporting large-scale transportation operations within an airport or similarly complex environment, where safety, reliability, and passenger service are critical.
Professional certifications in safety or security disciplines, such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Transit Safety & Security Program (TSSP), or similar credentials.
Experience supervising professional staff members.

About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

Engineering, integration, and cybersecurity support to design, build, and test enhanced services for the Department of Navy's IT architecture. Offers a wide range of roles, from cybersecurity experts to engineers specializing in systems, networks, software, and data center services.

About The Role

Peraton is seeking an Information Systems Security Manager to support out customer onsite in Washington D.C. who will be responsible for the following but not limited to:

Manage and oversee the security posture of all information systems. Implement and enforce security policies, procedures, and best practices to ensure system integrity and confidentiality.
Lead the process of certifying and accrediting information systems in accordance with the Risk Management Framework(s) (RMF) and other applicable government cybersecurity standards. Ensure systems meet required security controls for authorization to operate (ATO).
Perform risk assessments, vulnerability scans, and security audits to identify security risks and weaknesses in information systems. Develop and implement mitigation strategies to address identified risks and ensure ongoing compliance with security standards.
Ensure compliance with relevant cybersecurity frameworks, such as FISMA, NIST SP 800-53, and RMF, and ensure all systems supporting operations follow federal and DoD information assurance requirements.
Oversee incident response activities related to information security breaches, including root cause analysis, containment, remediation, and reporting. Work with the security team and stakeholders to manage cybersecurity incidents and minimize their impact on operations.
Implement and manage continuous monitoring of information systems and networks to detect and respond to potential security threats. Ensure all systems are regularly tested for security vulnerabilities.
Maintain accurate and comprehensive documentation of security controls, certifications, accreditation reports, and incident responses. Prepare regular security reports and updates for management and program leadership.
Work closely with engineering teams, mission planners, IT specialists, and other stakeholders to integrate cybersecurity into all phases of system design, development, and operations. Serve as the point of contact for information security issues related to information systems.
Develop and implement training programs for ISSO and ISSE personnel on information assurance and security best practices. Conduct cybersecurity awareness campaigns to ensure all team members understand their role in protecting sensitive data and systems.
Manage relationships with external vendors, contractors, and partners to ensure their systems and operations comply with information assurance requirements for the program.
Ensure compliance with protection requirements, control procedures, incident management reporting, remote access requirements, and system management for all systems within the enterprise.
Ensure the day-to-day implementation, oversight, continuous monitoring, and maintenance of the security configuration, practices, and procedures for each IS
Provide liaison support between the system owner, ISSOs, ISSEs, and other IS security personnel
Provides technical and programmatic information assurance services to internal and external customers in support of network and information security systems.
Designs, develops, and implements security requirements within an organization's business processes.
Prepares documentation from information obtained from customer using accepted guidelines.
Prepares security test and evaluation plans.
Provides certification and accreditation support in the development of security and contingency plans and conducts complex risk and vulnerability assessments.
Analyzes policies and procedures against Federal laws and regulations and provides recommendations for closing gaps.
Recommends system enhancements to improve security deficiencies.
Develops, tests, and integrates computer and network security tools.
Secures system configurations and installs security tools, scans systems to determine compliancy and report results and evaluates products and various aspects of system administration.
Conducts security program audits and develops solutions to lessen identified risks.
Provides information assurance support for the development and implementation of security architectures to meet new and evolving security requirements.
Provides assistance in computer incident investigations. Performs vulnerability assessments including development of risk mitigation strategies.

Must possess an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility.
Minimum of 12 years with BS/BA; Minimum of 10 years with MS/MA; Minimum of 16 years of experience in Information Systems security may be considered in lieu of degree.
Proven ISSM experience including knowledge of system functions, cybersecurity policies, and technical cybersecurity protection measures.
IAM Level III certification required.
Experience with A&A package submission

The National Airspace System is one of the world's most sophisticated and mission-critical infrastructures
, and the systems supporting it must perform reliably every day.

As a Project Manager supporting Surveillance and Radar Systems, you will help lead the people, processes, and technology behind critical aviation capabilities. Your leadership will help teams respond to evolving requirements, manage complex initiatives, reduce risk, and deliver solutions that strengthen the safety, efficiency, and readiness of the nation's airspace.

At Peraton, you won't just manage projects-you'll help shape the future of air traffic management.

Qualifications

U.S. Citizenship required.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.
Bachelor's degree with 8 years of experience, Master's with 6 years, Associate's with 10 years, or HS diploma/equivalent with 12 years of relevant experience.
Proven project leadership experience supporting Surveillance and/or Radar Systems, including surface surveillance, sensor data feeds, multi-sensor fusion, primary/secondary radar, SSR, ASR, or similar systems.

Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Risk Operations GTM Enablement
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Risk PMO team protects Stripe’s revenue and drives cross-functional strategy for company-level and org-level priorities. As Stripe operates across an increasingly complex and fast-moving global regulatory environment, one of our most important functions is ensuring that our largest, most strategic users can grow with us—compliantly, confidently, and at speed.

We sit at the intersection of Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and GTM—serving as the bridge between teams coordinating massive programs with global, wide-reaching impact. We build durable systems that enable strong collaboration across functions and seamless experiences for our users.

If you're energized by high-stakes, ambiguous problems and thrive on building programs from scratch in environments where the rules are still being written—we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

You will define, own, and execute program strategies for large-scale regulatory initiatives, operating with significant autonomy across a portfolio of global projects.

This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor (IC) role. While you will influence senior leadership and set strategic direction, you are also the primary driver of execution. You will need to zoom out to design the long-term vision, and zoom in to manage the details—building templates, tracking deliverables, writing documentation, and directly unblocking cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

Own and execute high-stakes global programs end-to-end, from initial strategy and scoping to project planning, day-to-day tracking, and change management
Drive step-change improvements in our operational processes, rolling up your sleeves to build systems and workflows that directly improve business outcomes and top-line metrics
Bridge compliance and commercial strategy by partnering with GTM and account leadership to turn complex regulatory requirements into a competitive advantage that builds deep user trust
Build and run operating models across diverse cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance), keeping highly distributed workstreams aligned and accountable
Serve as a trusted advisor by preparing strategic reviews for senior stakeholders and managing critical escalations
Translate user friction into program evolution by establishing structured, data-driven approaches to gather user feedback and turning those insights into actionable product and operational improvements
Diagnose and resolve systemic operational gaps before they impact our users, building self-healing processes and scalable internal infrastructure
Champion Stripe’s Operating Principles by fostering a high-performance culture that values rigorous thinking, rapid execution, and putting users first

Who you are

You are a highly strategic operator, a masterful communicator, and a systems thinker with operational grit. You thrive in the gray area, possessing the ability to translate ambiguous global challenges into elegant, structured, and highly actionable operational frameworks.

You are a natural leader who leads by influence and by example. You have a deep empathy for the user, an unyielding bias toward action, and you take pride in the craft of execution. No problem is too complex for you to deconstruct, and no detail is too small if it impacts the user experience.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of experience in Program Management, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, or Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
Hands-on execution track record: Proven ability to work independently as an individual contributor, managing complex, multi-stakeholder project plans and deliverables from inception to completion
Exceptional communication & storytelling: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to distill highly complex, technical, or regulatory topics into clear, succinct, and persuasive narratives to external and senior audiences
Systems and infrastructure builder: Deep experience designing, launching, and scaling complex cross-functional operating models, feedback loops, and PMO frameworks
Growth mindset: A high willingness to learn, adapt quickly to changing environments, and actively seek and act on feedback to continuously improve

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in high-growth technology or fintech environments
Deep cross-functional partnership: Prior experience working alongside Engineering, Product, Legal, Compliance, and GTM/Sales
Data fluency: Experience leveraging data visualization tools and analytical frameworks to back up strategic decisions and measure program success

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Please find our California applicant personal information notice here.

The application window will remain open for 100 days after the Job Post is published. However, this opportunity will remain open based on the needs of the business, which may cause the application window to close before or after the 100-day mark.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager & Test Lead (Hybrid Agile / Waterfall)
new_jobs.description:
At Capgemini Engineering, the world leader in engineering services, we bring together a global team of engineers, scientists, and architects to help the world’s most innovative companies unleash their potential. From autonomous cars to life-saving robots, our digital and software technology experts think outside the box as they provide unique R&D and engineering services across all industries. Join us for a career full of opportunities. Where you can make a difference. Where no two days are the same.

Job Description

Context & Mission Background

A leading global manufacturing and life sciences organization is executing a worldwide digital transformation program to replace legacy paper and decentralized Permit-to-Work (PTW) workflows with a unified, cloud-based Enterprise Electronic Permit-to-Work (E-PTW) SaaS solution.

The program encompasses a global rollout across dozens of production, R&D, and tertiary facilities, onboarding 20,000+ internal personnel and contractor partners. The platform integrates with enterprise ERP/CMMS and cloud data lake architectures.

Delivery Governance:
Hybrid Model

Waterfall Program Governance: Multi-wave deployment gates, compliance sign-offs, centralized testing gates, and transition to steady-state Run/Support.
Agile Sprints: Iterative core-model build, configuration sprints, interface testing, and continuous feedback loops.

Role Overview

The Project Manager & Test Lead will orchestrate the global multi-wave deployment while establishing, structuring, and leading the Centralized Testing & Quality Assurance Workstream (Core Model validation, System Integration Testing / SIT, and centralized User Acceptance Testing / UAT).

Key Responsibilities

Hybrid Program & Multi-Wave Governance
Lead global program execution across all deployment phases (Core Build, Pilot Phase, Multi-Wave Rollouts, and Handover to Run/AIMS).
Maintain the master project schedule, milestones, dependencies, budget envelope, and RAID log.
Facilitate Agile configuration ceremonies while enforcing Waterfall stage gates (Core Model Sign-Off, Centralized UAT Go/No-Go, Site Deployment Readiness, Hypercare Exit).
Align technical delivery milestones with the Change Management team’s ADKAR gate reviews.
Centralized Test Strategy & Testing Team Leadership
Define, govern, and execute the Centralized Test Strategy covering Unit, SIT, Core Model UAT, Non-Regression, and Interface/Data Testing.
Lead and coordinate the centralized test team, managing technical testers, business representatives, and vendor test engineers.
Define formal Entry/Exit criteria for Centralized UAT and manage defect triage workflows and SLA tracking in Jira.
Oversee integration and data-flow testing between the SaaS solution, enterprise ERP/CMMS systems, and enterprise data platforms.
Produce formal test summary reports and quality metrics for executive Steering Committees and formal deployment stage gates.
Vendor & Partner Delivery Management
Manage deliverables, technical backlogs, and commitments with the external SaaS provider and systems integrators.
Track enterprise dependencies including IAM/Single Sign-On and external contractor access frameworks.

Candidate Profile & Qualifications

Experience: 7+ years in Project Management within global manufacturing, chemical, pharmaceutical, or regulated industrial environments.
Methodology: Proven track record in Hybrid delivery (PMP / PRINCE2 combined with Agile / Scrum / SAFe).
Testing Leadership: 4+ years leading testing teams and managing structured test lifecycles (ISTQB certification or equivalent practical expertise).
Tooling: Advanced proficiency in Jira, Confluence, test management and familiarity with enterprise ERP/CMMS ecosystems.

new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Risk PMO team protects Stripe’s revenue and drives cross-functional strategy for company-level and org-level priorities. As Stripe operates across an increasingly complex and fast-moving global regulatory environment, one of our most important functions is ensuring that our largest, most strategic users can grow with us—compliantly, confidently, and at speed.

We sit at the intersection of Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and GTM—serving as the bridge between teams coordinating massive programs with global, wide-reaching impact. We build durable systems that enable strong collaboration across functions and seamless experiences for our users.

If you're energized by high-stakes, ambiguous problems and thrive on building programs from scratch in environments where the rules are still being written—we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

You will define, own, and execute program strategies for large-scale regulatory initiatives, operating with significant autonomy across a portfolio of global projects.

This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor (IC) role. While you will influence senior leadership and set strategic direction, you are also the primary driver of execution. You will need to zoom out to design the long-term vision, and zoom in to manage the details—building templates, tracking deliverables, writing documentation, and directly unblocking cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

Own and execute high-stakes global programs end-to-end, from initial strategy and scoping to project planning, day-to-day tracking, and change management
Drive step-change improvements in our operational processes, rolling up your sleeves to build systems and workflows that directly improve business outcomes and top-line metrics
Bridge compliance and commercial strategy by partnering with GTM and account leadership to turn complex regulatory requirements into a competitive advantage that builds deep user trust
Build and run operating models across diverse cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance), keeping highly distributed workstreams aligned and accountable
Serve as a trusted advisor by preparing strategic reviews for senior stakeholders and managing critical escalations
Translate user friction into program evolution by establishing structured, data-driven approaches to gather user feedback and turning those insights into actionable product and operational improvements
Diagnose and resolve systemic operational gaps before they impact our users, building self-healing processes and scalable internal infrastructure
Champion Stripe’s Operating Principles by fostering a high-performance culture that values rigorous thinking, rapid execution, and putting users first

Who you are

You are a highly strategic operator, a masterful communicator, and a systems thinker with operational grit. You thrive in the gray area, possessing the ability to translate ambiguous global challenges into elegant, structured, and highly actionable operational frameworks.

You are a natural leader who leads by influence and by example. You have a deep empathy for the user, an unyielding bias toward action, and you take pride in the craft of execution. No problem is too complex for you to deconstruct, and no detail is too small if it impacts the user experience.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of experience in Program Management, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, or Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
Hands-on execution track record: Proven ability to work independently as an individual contributor, managing complex, multi-stakeholder project plans and deliverables from inception to completion
Exceptional communication & storytelling: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to distill highly complex, technical, or regulatory topics into clear, succinct, and persuasive narratives to external and senior audiences
Systems and infrastructure builder: Deep experience designing, launching, and scaling complex cross-functional operating models, feedback loops, and PMO frameworks
Growth mindset: A high willingness to learn, adapt quickly to changing environments, and actively seek and act on feedback to continuously improve

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in high-growth technology or fintech environments
Deep cross-functional partnership: Prior experience working alongside Engineering, Product, Legal, Compliance, and GTM/Sales
Data fluency: Experience leveraging data visualization tools and analytical frameworks to back up strategic decisions and measure program success

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Please find our California applicant personal information notice here.

The application window will remain open for 100 days after the Job Post is published. However, this opportunity will remain open based on the needs of the business, which may cause the application window to close before or after the 100-day mark.

Keyrus is an international group of 2,800 consultants and experts across 28 countries, built on a single conviction: AI does not transform businesses. Architected intelligence does.

Over time, you grow into one of the rarest professionals of the intelligence era: someone who bridges data, AI, and human decision-making at scale, across industries and geographies. Technology amplifies. Keyrus culture differentiates. Industrial discipline connects the two.

Full-time

while aligning business and technology teams around clear strategic objectives. - someone who thinks like an architect and acts like a builder.

Ensure effective collaboration between business, product, engineering, and AI delivery teams within remote and international environments.

👤
Who You Are

You are curious, analytical, and motivated by solving meaningful business challenges.

Proven experience delivering AI transformation initiatives and/or enterprise technology programs

Professional proficiency in English.

Strong expertise in Project and Program Management
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and negotiation skills
Strong governance, planning, risk management, and executive reporting capabilities
Ability to translate business objectives into delivery roadmaps and measurable outcomes
Experience coordinating business, product, engineering, and delivery teams
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities
Familiarity with Agile and hybrid delivery methodologies
Business-focused mindset combined with sufficient technical fluency to collaborate effectively with technical teams

Nice to Have

Experience delivering AI Agent initiatives or other applied AI transformation programs
Experience with Sales & Marketing transformation projects
Experience working with Salesforce programs and the broader Salesforce ecosystem
Exposure to Microsoft Copilot, Power Platform, Dynamics 365, or Azure AI
Experience in consulting or client-facing environments
Experience working in remote, multicultural, and international teams
Project Management certifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, AgilePM, SAFe, or equivalent qualifications.

⭐
What Makes You Successful

You focus on outcomes rather than activity.
You approach challenges with curiosity and pragmatism.
You communicate complex concepts in a clear and accessible way.
You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and finding practical solutions.
You contribute to collective intelligence by sharing knowledge and supporting others.
You combine autonomy with collaboration.
You continuously look for opportunities to improve systems, processes, and results.

🎁
What We Offer at Keyrus Spain

Competitive salary, paid in 14 instalments (option for 12 from day one).
Annual performance bonus.
Meal allowance (Restaurant Tickets): €1,800/year net, distributed over 11 monthly reloads

Private medical insurance with Sanitas (no copays, dental included)

December 24th and 31st are considered company holidays when they fall on working days

A collaborative, international, and human-centred work environment

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

About The Role

Peraton is currently seeking skilled and qualified candidates for a Program Manager
position to provide overall program leadership and serve as the single point of accountability for contractor performance supporting Peraton and the customer. The Program Manager will oversee program execution across all four contract task areas, ensuring performance meets contractual requirements, schedules, quality standards, and customer expectations.

You will lead program planning, governance, stakeholder engagement, Agile execution, transition activities, subcontractor management, and performance reporting. The Program Manager will serve as the primary interface with the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC), Contracting Officer/Contracting Officer's Representative (CO/COR), and Government stakeholders.

The Program Manager will ensure effective coordination across contractor teams and subcontractors, maintain program visibility through management dashboards and reporting, and drive timely resolution of schedule, staffing, cost, performance, and operational issues.

Day to Day Work Responsibilities:

Serve as the single point of accountability to the customer POC for all contractor performance across all four contract task areas.
Schedule, coordinate, and host the Project Kick-Off Meeting, ensuring participation by all required Key Personnel.
Convene and chair monthly Technical Status Meetings with customer and Government stakeholders.
Develop, deliver, and maintain the Monthly Status Report (MSR), including personnel gains and losses, cost by Contract Line Item Number (CLIN), schedule status, program performance, and corrective actions.
Develop, maintain, and continuously update the Project Management Plan (PMP) and Agile Roadmap, incorporating Government feedback and comments.
Provide monthly Agile Roadmap briefings covering 30-, 60-, and 90-day schedules, critical dependencies, milestones, and schedule risks.
Oversee and coordinate all contractor travel authorizations and Trip Report submissions.
Maintain the Management Dashboard with real-time or near-real-time program, personnel, schedule, cost, and performance data.
Lead Transition-In execution and ensure all required transition activities are completed within 90 calendar days of the Project Kick-Off.
Develop and deliver the Transition-Out Plan within six months of performance start and implement the plan no later than six months before contract expiration.
Manage and oversee subcontractor performance, other program teammates.
Monitor program execution across multiple workstreams to ensure contractual requirements, milestones, deliverables, and performance objectives are achieved.
Identify, assess, and communicate program risks, issues, dependencies, and corrective actions to Government and contractor leadership.
Establish and maintain effective program governance, communication, reporting, and escalation processes.
Coordinate cross-functional contractor resources to ensure successful execution of program requirements and delivery commitments.
Apply Agile program management practices to support iterative planning, execution, prioritization, and delivery.
Ensure program documentation, status reporting, schedules, roadmaps, and management artifacts remain accurate, current, and compliant with contractual requirements.
Monitor staffing, personnel changes, cost performance, schedule performance, and other program metrics to identify potential impacts to contract execution.
Drive continuous process improvement across program management, reporting, transition, governance, and stakeholder engagement activities.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
U.S. Citizenship required.
Must be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret (TS) security clearance and a DEA suitability determination.
10+ years of IT program and/or project management experience.
5+ years of experience managing programs of comparable scope and complexity; experience with programs exceeding $100M in annual contract value preferred
PMP Certification
ITIL v4 Foundation or higher certification
SAFe Agilist or SAFe Program Consultant certification
Demonstrated experience managing multiple workstreams, contractor teams, and subcontractors within a complex federal IT environment.
Experience developing and managing Program Management Plans, Agile Roadmaps, schedules, status reports, risk registers, and other program management artifacts.
Experience leading Government-facing meetings, briefings, program reviews, and executive-level communications.

Join our Vanguard 401(k) plan, with immediate vesting and a generous company match to help you build long-term financial security. Our team also enjoys 10 paid company holidays, a generous PTO accrual schedule, and access to discounts on useful products and services.

This Opportunity:

The Program Manager will lead a regional team of Project Managers responsible for delivering a high-volume portfolio of inside plant cabling projects within data center environments. This role is accountable for PM team performance, regional project execution, forecasting accuracy, schedule adherence, cost control, change management, documentation discipline, and client satisfaction.

The Program Manager will oversee a regional pipeline of approximately 15-30 active projects, with 4-8 new project starts per month, and will ensure Project Managers have the direction, support, resources, and accountability needed to deliver projects safely, on time, within budget, and in alignment with customer requirements. Promote company Core Values to foster and safeguard Company culture

Provideaccurateandtimelyproject forecasting to support regional planning and resource allocation decisions
Activelyparticipatesin client and project interviews for new contracts and continuing business opportunities as may berequired

Proven ability to lead Project Managers in a fast-paced, high-volume project environment
Strong understanding of datacenter, structured cabling, low-voltage, fiber, copper, pathway, rack/cabinet, labeling, testing, and closeout requirements
Ability to manage a multi-project regional portfolio without losing visibility into safety, schedule, cost, quality, documentation, risk, or customer commitments
Strong organizational skills and the ability to create structure, cadence, and accountability across multiple Project Managers and field teams
Proficient in using project data, dashboards, job cost reports, forecasts, schedules, and PM updates to make informed business decisions
Solid understanding of projectfinancial management, including job cost tracking, forecasting, margin maintenance, billing status, change order management, and cost-to-complete analysis
Knowledge of safety protocols, customer site policies, and work practices applicable to datacenterand mission-critical environments
Ability toidentifychange events early and ensure Project Managers follow disciplined change management practices
Ability to develop, review, and manage project schedules across a concurrent project portfolio
Demonstrated professionalism and ability to communicate effectively with executives, customers, Project Managers, field supervision, vendors, subcontractors, and craft personnel
Ability to work under time constraints, respond to changing requirements, andmaintaina positive,solutions-focused leadership style
Strong oral and written communication skills, including clear customer updates, internal escalation, meeting leadership, and documentation review
Disciplined, detail oriented, organized, self-driven, and comfortable owning results through others
Demonstrated ability to resolve complex scheduling conflicts, scope issues, site coordination challenges, customer escalations, and resource constraints
Proficient with Microsoft Office applications and project/job cost platforms such as Procore, Bluebeam, Viewpoint Vista, or similar systems
Entrepreneurial mindset witha high levelof motivation and the ability tooperateindependently while building alignment across the team

Experience and Education:

High school diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor’s degree in construction management, business, engineering, information technology, telecommunications, or a related discipline is a plus, but equivalent hands-on data center, cabling, low-voltage, or field leadership experience will be given full consideration
Minimum5+ years of project or program delivery experience, preferably in datacenter, structured cabling, low-voltage, telecommunications, fiber/copper infrastructure, or mission-critical environments
Experience leading Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, Project Coordinators, field leaders, or multi-project delivery teams is strongly preferred
Demonstrated experience managing or overseeing multiple concurrent projects at various stages of intake, planning, execution, closeout, and billing

Experience managing projects across common contract delivery methods, including lump sum/fixed price, unit price/rate, and time and material
Proven ability to use project management, scheduling, reporting, or job cost systems to manage a multi-project workload and provideaccurateforecasts
OSHA-30 Hour certificationrequired. If not certified at time of hire, certification must be obtained within the first six (6) months of employment

Regional role with willingness to commit to approximately 25% travel within the assigned region, including customer sites, project locations, regional offices, and team meetings as needed.

Job Summary: The Senior Program Manager serves as the primary customer interface and point of contact accountable for ensuring programs meet cost, schedule, and performance requirements. This role provides guidance and solutions to program teams in ways that promote PDA’s culture, oversees the progress of program operations, and leads staff across multiple disciplines to deliver results in a timely manner. The Senior Program Manager also develops efficient strategies and tactics directed at growing the business.
Responsibilities: ·       Direct and coordinate program activities, leading and motivating teams to complete assigned work on time, to specification, and with accuracy and efficiency.
·       Address customer questions, concerns, and complaints throughout the program, and serve as an intake point for issues between scheduled reviews so that nothing affecting scope, schedule, cost, or deliverables is held until the next meeting.
·       Plan and manage program milestones, deadlines, and activities, including maintaining and updating the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) and tracking deliverable status across functional groups.
·       Manage Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) due dates and submission tracking with a zero-miss standard.
·       Manage program budgets and cost accounts, control expenditures in accordance with budget allocations, develop Estimates at Completion (EAC), and prepare written explanations of cost variances (labor hours and dollars expended against authorized budgets).
·       Identify and manage program risks, issues, and opportunities; proactively flag schedule risks and develop mitigation plans.

·       Review reports and records of program activities to track progress toward program objectives, adjust methodology as needed, and assess program performance periodically and at completion.
·       Schedule and facilitate meetings with agendas and defined goals; prepare meeting minutes, weekly status reports, and formal correspondence.
·       Participate in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) and technical reviews (e.g., System Requirements Review, Critical Design Review).

·       Perform other related duties as assigned.

·       Familiarity with government contract management fundamentals, including Contract Work Breakdown Structure (CWBS) development and subcontract management practices.
·       Working knowledge of Configuration Management (CM) processes and Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) / Configuration Control Board (CCB) workflows.
·       Excellent knowledge of MS Office Suite; working knowledge of project management software (e.g., MS Project, Basecamp) is a strong advantage.
·       Experience with earned value management (EVM) or similar cost/schedule performance measurement systems is preferred.

Core Competencies: ·       Understanding of company goals and objectives
·       Strong written and oral communication skills
·       Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, external customers, and other stakeholders
·       Outstanding leadership and organizational skills, including demonstrated supervisory or coaching experience
·       Understanding of customer requirements
·       Willingness to self-develop and maintain additional skills required to perform position

Join a dynamic team driving large-scale Siemens Teamcenter PLM transformation programs for leading global organizations including PLM implementation, enhancement, and transformation initiatives.

Candidates should be strong project leaders capable of driving complex, cross-functional programs involving business, engineering, IT, and vendor teams.

Coordinate business, engineering, IT, and third-party vendor teams to drive seamless collaboration and ensure successful program execution.

3 - 5+ years of project management experience delivering complex enterprise technology, transformation, or engineering-related programs.
